alt: A search for the smallest input on which a wrong attempt disagrees with a brute force. Inputs are tried shortest first in a fixed order, each shown as an array beside a row comparing the two answers, with runs of matching inputs skipped. The first disagreement is shown, then the repaired attempt agreeing with the brute force.

steps.caption: Input 1, [0]. The brute force says 1 and the attempt says 1. They match.
The rest of the inputs of length 1 also match (inputs 2 to 3). The last of them is [2].
Input 4, [0, 0]. The brute force says 1 and the attempt says 1. They match.
The rest of the inputs of length 2 also match (inputs 5 to 12). The last of them is [2, 2].
Input 13, [0, 0, 0]. The brute force says 1 and the attempt says 1. They match.
Input 14, [0, 0, 1]. The brute force says 2 and the attempt says 1. They differ: this is the smallest failing input, found in size order.

On [0, 0, 1] the brute force finds the increasing run 0, 1 of length 2. The attempt returns 1: at the repeated 0 it reset run to 0, so the 1 that followed only brought it back to 1. A new run already holds the current value, so it should restart at 1.
With run reset to 1, the attempt returns 2 on [0, 0, 1], matching the brute force. Over all 39 inputs, the fixed attempt never differs from the brute force.
